what: Three dead after volcano erupts on Indonesian island

clean_source_blocks.text: Three people hiking on Indonesia's Mount Dukono have died after the volcano erupted on Friday morning. Videos and pictures of the eruption show the volcano, located on North Maluku island, spewing a column of ash stretching 10km (six miles) into the sky. The three victims were part of a group of 20 Singaporeans and Indonesians hiking on the mountain despite restrictions. The rest of the group was eventually located by rescuers and evacuated from the mountain. The volcano has erupted more than 200 times since last March. Officials had previously issued warnings against climbing the mountain due to safety concerns. The latest eruption took place at 07:41 local time (22:41 GMT Thursday), when there were several people on the mountain on early morning hikes.
Officials had previously issued warnings on climbing the active volcano due to safety concerns.

Two Singaporeans and local person were in a no-go zone when they were killed, say officials Three hikers – two Singaporeans and an Indonesian – have died in an eruption of Indonesia’s Mount Dukono volcano, where they found themselves in a no-go zone, officials said. The eruption, on Halmahera island, sent an ash cloud about 6 miles (10km) into the air, with no towns of villages near enough to face any immediate threat. Twenty hikers were on the slopes when disaster struck, the North Halmahera police chief, Erlichson Pasaribu, told reporters at a volcano monitoring station in Mamuya village. Nine were from Singapore and the rest Indonesian. “To date, 15 climbers have safely descended,” Erlichson said several hours after the early-morning eruption.

North Halmahera police chief Erlichson Pasaribu said that retrieval of the bodies, which are located at higher elevations, has been hampered by repeated eruptions, difficult terrain and strong blasts from the volcano. Besides the 20-member hiking group, eyewitness accounts indicate there were other hikers on the mountain as well. One guide who was on Mount Dukono with two clients at the time of the eruption told BBC Indonesian that he believed high pressure had been building up inside the volcano for several days. "When Dukono hasn't erupted for a few days, you have to be careful," he said, describing the eruption as "major" and "very strong". As they were hiking up, he saw one group of people at the edge of the crater, as well as another group about 50m from the crater who were filming drone videos.

Indonesian officials said two Singaporeans and one local resident from the nearby city of Ternate had died.

Rescuers eventually located the rest of their hiking group. Most of them were safely evacuated from the mountain and sent to a hospital to have their injuries treated.

Two members of the group, who are porters, stayed behind on the mountain to help rescue workers locate the bodies.

Three hikers – two Singaporeans and an Indonesian – have died in an eruption of Indonesia’s Mount Dukono volcano, where they found themselves in a no-go zone, officials said.

The eruption, on Halmahera island, sent an ash cloud about 6 miles (10km) into the air, with no towns of villages near enough to face any immediate threat.

Twenty hikers were on the slopes when disaster struck, the North Halmahera police chief, Erlichson Pasaribu, told reporters at a volcano monitoring station in Mamuya village. Nine were from Singapore and the rest Indonesian.

“To date, 15 climbers have safely descended,” Erlichson said several hours after the early-morning eruption.

The bodies of the dead hikers were still on the mountain, he said, without elaborating on the whereabouts of the remaining two. “Due to ongoing eruptions, the situation is still considered unsafe for evacuation. So, the joint team is still waiting for the right time to begin the search,” Erlichson said.

Some of the hikers had minor injuries and were taken to hospital for treatment. The group’s guide and a porter were taken to the police station and could face criminal charges for taking hikers into a prohibited area, said the police chief.

Since December, the national volcanology centre has been warning tourists and climbers not to come within two and half miles (4km) of the volcano’s Malupang Warirang crater after scientists spotted an increase in seismic activity.

Erlichson said the hikers had ignored social media appeals and warning signs put up at the entrance of the trail to stay away. “Local residents understand and don’t want to climb. Many [hikers] are foreign tourists who wish to create content,” he said.

It could be dangerous for public health, Lana said, and risked disrupting transportation services. There are no settlements within a radius of about five and half miles (9km) from the volcano.

payload.title: Kolme vaeltajaa kuoli tulivuoren purkauksessa Indonesiassa
payload.summary: Kolme Mount Dukonolla vaeltanutta ihmistä on kuollut tulivuoren purkauduttua Indonesian Halmaheran saarella. Viranomaisten mukaan ryhmä oli alueella, jonne menemisestä oli varoitettu turvallisuussyistä.
payload.content:
Kolme vaeltajaa on kuollut Mount Dukonon tulivuoren purkauksessa Indonesian Halmaheran saarella perjantaiaamuna paikallista aikaa. Viranomaisten mukaan uhrit kuuluivat 20 hengen vaellusryhmään, jossa oli singaporelaisia ja indonesialaisia, ja ryhmä oli liikkunut vuorella rajoituksista huolimatta aktiiviselle tulivuorelle annetuista turvallisuusvaroituksista huolimatta.

## Purkaus nosti tuhkapilven korkealle

Purkaus tapahtui kello 7.41 paikallista aikaa eli torstaina kello 22.41 GMT-aikaa. Kuvissa ja videoilla tulivuori syöksee ilmaan noin 10 kilometrin korkuisen tuhkapatsaan. Viranomaisten mukaan lähistöllä ei ollut kaupunkeja tai kyliä, joihin purkaus olisi aiheuttanut välitöntä uhkaa.

Kuolleet olivat viranomaistietojen mukaan kaksi singaporelaista ja yksi indonesialainen. Pohjois-Halmaheran poliisipäällikkö Erlichson Pasaribu kertoi, että vuoren rinteillä oli purkauksen aikaan 20 vaeltajaa. Heistä yhdeksän oli Singaporesta ja loput Indonesiasta. Uhreja kuvattiin olleen alueella, jonne ei olisi pitänyt mennä.

## Pelastustyöt jatkuivat vaikeissa oloissa

Pelastajat paikansivat loput ryhmästä ja evakuoivat heidät vuorelta. Useita vaeltajia pääsi laskeutumaan turvallisesti alas jo purkauksen jälkeisten tuntien aikana. Pasaribun mukaan 15 kiipeilijää oli päässyt turvallisesti alas useita tunteja varhaisaamun purkauksen jälkeen.

Ruumiiden noutamista on viranomaisten mukaan vaikeuttanut se, että ne sijaitsevat ylempänä vuorella. Työtä ovat hidastaneet myös toistuvat purkaukset, vaikeakulkuinen maasto ja tulivuoresta purkautuvat voimakkaat paineaallot.

## Vuorelle oli annettu varoituksia

Viranomaiset olivat varoittaneet Mount Dukonolle kiipeämisestä jo ennen onnettomuutta, koska kyseessä on aktiivinen tulivuori. Vuori on purkautunut yli 200 kertaa viime vuoden maaliskuun jälkeen.

Silminnäkijähavaintojen perusteella vuorella saattoi olla vaellusryhmän lisäksi muitakin ihmisiä. Eräs opas kertoi olleensa Mount Dukonolla kahden asiakkaan kanssa purkauksen aikaan. Hänen mukaansa tulivuoren sisälle oli voinut kertyä painetta useiden päivien ajan.

Opas kertoi nähneensä ihmisiä kraatterin reunalla sekä toisen ryhmän noin 50 metrin päässä kraatterista kuvaamassa dronevideoita. Hän kuvaili purkausta suureksi ja erittäin voimakkaaksi ja sanoi, että Dukonolla on oltava varovainen, jos se ei ole purkautunut muutamaan päivään.

One guide who was on Mount Dukono with two clients at the time of the eruption told BBC Indonesian that he believed high pressure had been building up inside the volcano for several days. "When Dukono hasn't erupted for a few days, you have to be careful," he said, describing the eruption as "major" and "very strong". As they were hiking up, he saw one group of people at the edge of the crater, as well as another group about 50m from the crater who were filming drone videos.
